data.narrative:
TerraFirma is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $115M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparable companies—one public and eight private—spanning the same sector and adjacent funding stages, including Series A leaders like Humanoid ($1.4B) and Series B performers such as Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B) and Generalist AI ($2.0B).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy base and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A forward, yields $230M. Peer-median analysis across the five most relevant comparables (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Humanoid, and Walden Robotics) produces $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B.

Triangulating these methods produces a low-end estimate of $196M, a median of $940M, and a high-end scenario of $1.9B. The substantial spread reflects stage compression in the peer set—some comparables trade at Series B valuations while TerraFirma remains at Series A. Key uncertainties include whether peer multiples will contract in a harder fundraising environment and whether TerraFirma's capital efficiency and technical differentiation warrant a premium or discount relative to the median cohort. The $940M median represents a reasonable central case absent material new information on unit economics or market traction.
